text.p: Swedish commercial bank Swedbank is expected to post a profit after credit losses of 3.65 billion crowns for the first nine months of 1996, a Reuters poll of 11 analysts found on Wednesday.
In the corresponding period a year ago the bank reported a profit after credit losses of 2.98 billion crowns.
The average of forecasts for credit losses was 1.34 billion crowns compared with 1.80 billion a year ago.
For the full year 1996 Swedbank was expected to report a profit of 4.85 billion crowns after credit losses compared to 1.74 billion crowns.
In 1995 the bank's profit was 4.31 billion crowns.
Analysts' forecasts for credit losses for the nine months varied between 1.22 billion and 1.45 billion crowns and between 1.58-2.00 billion for calendar 1996.
The average forecast for profit after credit losses in 1997 was 5.01 billion crowns. Forecasts were between 4.43 billion and 5.72 billion crowns.
For 1998 analysts forecast a profit of 5.19 billion crowns on average. Forecasts varied between 4.42 and 6.11 billion crowns.
Analysts interviewed for the poll were from Enskilda, Morgan Stanley, SBC Warburg, Ohman, Penser, Fiba Nordic, Aragon, Handelsbanken Markets, Aros, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and Carnegie.
Swedbank's nine month report is due for release on November 6.
